title: Leaderless Quorum
explain: A leaderless quorum defines how many replicas must respond for a read or write to count, in a replica set with no leader. You do not need everyone, only a minimum number of votes: W for writes and R for reads. If W + R > N, every read overlaps every successful write on at least one replica.
model:
My framing: with no leader, define success by a minimum vote count instead of by everyone.

```
N = 3 replicas   W = 2   R = 2     (W + R = 4 > 3)
write set: {A,B}        read set: {B,C}   ─▶ overlap at B ─▶ sees newest version
```

**The rule: W + R > N.** Then any read set and any successful write set share at least one replica, and with version comparison the read returns the newest acknowledged write.

Tuning:

- **Majority:** W = R = floor(N/2) + 1; tolerates floor((N−1)/2) failures.
- **W = N, R = 1:** fast reads, but one node down blocks writes.
- **W = 1, R = N:** fast writes, but reads need everyone.
- **W + R ≤ N:** reads may miss the latest write: faster and more available, eventually consistent only.

**Not guaranteed even when W + R > N:** sloppy quorums (hinted handoff to nodes outside the replica set), failed writes that landed on some replicas, concurrent writes and clock-based LWW, and a replica restored from an old backup.

This is not linearizability, and replicas still need [repair](#/sd/f/leaderless-repair). See the [write path](#/sd/f/leaderless-write-path), [read path](#/sd/f/leaderless-read-path), and [quorum-based replication](#/sd/f/quorum-based-replication).

details.q: Why does W + R > N give overlap?
details.a: A write set of size W and a read set of size R drawn from N replicas must share a member when W + R > N (pigeonhole). That member has the acknowledged write, so the read can see it.

details.q: N = 5 and W = 3. What is the smallest R that guarantees overlap?
details.a: R = 3, since 3 + 3 = 6 > 5. R = 2 gives 5, which is not greater than N, so a read could miss the write.

details.q: N = 5, W = 4, R = 2: how many replicas can be down with both reads and writes still working?
details.a: One. Writes need 4 live replicas, so at most 1 can be down; reads need 2 so tolerate 3. The cluster's tolerance for both is the smaller, 1.

details.q: N = 3, W = 2, R = 1: a write is acked by A and B, then the client reads C alone. What happens?
details.a: It may get the old value. W + R = 3 is not greater than N = 3, so the read set {C} need not overlap the write set {A, B}.

details.q: With N = 3, W = 2, R = 2, what can still produce a stale read?
details.a: Sloppy quorums and hinted handoff, a failed write that partially landed, concurrent writes resolved by skewed LWW, and a replica restored from an old backup. Overlap is necessary, not sufficient.

details.q: A read-heavy store (99% reads, N = 3) needs fast and fresh reads. Which setting?
details.a: W = 3, R = 1: reads hit one replica and still see the latest, since every write reached all replicas. Cost: writes need every replica up, so one outage blocks writes.

prompts.q: State the quorum rule, why it works, and two cases where it still fails to give a fresh read.
points: Read and write sets must overlap in one replica
Failed or concurrent writes, clock-based LWW

prompts.q: Explain how you would tune W and R for a read-heavy vs a write-heavy store.
points: Read-heavy: W = N, R = 1, writes fragile
Write-heavy: W = 1, R = N, reads slow
W + R ≤ N: faster but eventual
Latency is the W-th / R-th fastest replica

prompts.q: Explain the difference between a leaderless quorum and a consensus quorum.
points: Leaderless: per-request W and R, no single history
Consensus: leader-ordered log committed on a majority
Leaderless is available but only mostly fresh
Consensus gives one history but stalls without a majority
